observations.trace: DeterministicRng uses fixed-width SplitMix64 and constructs a Rand Uniform for a NonZeroU64 upper bound. The exact locked Rand0.9.5 integer constructor rejects low>=high, and its constructed sampler uses a rejection loop; separate sample_single has a different bias policy. WeightedIndex<u64>::new checks empty input, zero total and checked sum overflow; an unsigned input cannot satisfy its negative-or-NaN InvalidWeight predicate. First-party SamplingError owns three error categories before the already recorded naming adapter stringifies them. The current movement-audio call passes SoundFamily::TAKES=3 to index.
observations.remaining: Prior e275 Lens1 recorded the same narrow native source rejection and nonempty audio precondition, not a global caller or randomness proof. Production expect calls at index, boolean and sample_below directly conflict with crates/AGENTS.md even where selected input makes their failure branches unreachable. index documents a nonempty caller precondition. Actual caller admission, compiler profile, feature resolution, final consumers and overall policy remain open. No RNG, hash, weighted sampler or test ran.

observations.trace: range_f32 checks both endpoints finite and minimum<=maximum, then computes minimum + unit*(maximum-minimum) in f32. For hypothetical -f32::MAX to +f32::MAX, each input meets that admission but the exact positive span is twice the largest finite f32. Under ordinary IEEE binary32 overflow semantics, the intermediate difference is infinite; with a hypothetical unit draw0, zero times infinity is NaN, and with a positive draw it is infinite. Earlier q662 already recorded this opposite-sign extreme-range issue as unresolved.
observations.remaining: No numerical operation, draw or test ran and no specific RNG seed or application caller has been shown to reach the extreme bounds. The current tactical spawn uses [-5,5], while selected strategic profile calls use small fixed spreads, so they do not establish the extreme witness. Equal endpoint, output upper-bound rounding and error policy remain design questions, not inferred new defects. This is separate from integer Uniform and prior MHR clamp.

observations.trace: StreamId wraps a nonempty static purpose; Seed derives a length-framed hash over root bytes, stream name and ordered context fields. StreamId::seed supplies fixed-width little-endian u64 context. Current source Hash feeds explicit canonical byte array, while Ord compares numeric words. Some distinct source sites intentionally repeat a stream purpose for the same underlying identity or phase; matching a String does not by itself prove an unwanted alias.
observations.remaining: No hash or random value was computed. Context slot identity, namespace reuse and all actual producers/consumers remain open. A blind derived Hash could change hasher input; any derive suggestion must preserve exact byte behavior. Native Rand0.8 integration remains the SpacetimeDB transaction boundary, not evidence of a legacy compatibility shim.
